lines.trans: Time for our ten-thousand-won premiere ratings pool, wishing for a smash hit!
Chief Producer Kim Tae-ho wrote seven percent? That is way too harsh!
Quite the opposite—since it will never sink to seven, it shows my resolve not to take your money!
And our youngest producer Baek Seung-chan wrote 6.8—not even seven?
Statistically, a season premiere rated about two points higher than the previous finale.
Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
Quit taking the wind out of our sails!
Look at our youngest writer—this is how a rookie should bet, brightly and positively!
Anyway, my gut feeling about this premiere is seriously great!
Please do not say that with too much confidence!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 첫방 시청률 만 원 내기다, 대박을 기원하면서!
examples.trans: Time for our ten-thousand-won premiere ratings pool, wishing for a smash hit!
Here the word for 'premiere broadcast' is key.
That drama has high viewer ratings.
The ratings went up a lot.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.
examples.trans: Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.
Here the word for 'within the span of' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun used with Sino-Korean numbers to state prices in South Korean won.

examples.trans: I only have a thousand won.
That is ten thousand won in total.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 첫방 시청률 만 원 내기다, 대박을 기원하면서!
examples.trans: Time for our ten-thousand-won premiere ratings pool, wishing for a smash hit!
Here the word for 'it is a bet' is key.
Did you hear about this big hit?
I was busy today because of big hit.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 첫방 시청률 만 원 내기다, 대박을 기원하면서!
examples.trans: Time for our ten-thousand-won premiere ratings pool, wishing for a smash hit!
This expression comes from 'praying for!'.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: So you two—the director and the chief producer—have to step in and shield her.
Here the word for 'the chief producer' is key.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral; used for percentages, dates, phone numbers, and scores

examples.trans: The ratings came out to seven percent.
July is summer.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
The atmosphere today is really was too much.
That person always looks was too much.

examples.text: 난 원래 미소천사인데 반대로 가야지. 천년보살 신디 어때?
examples.trans: I am already a smiling angel, so we should go the opposite way. How about Saintly Cindy?
The topic of in the opposite way came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 신디에겐 절대 비밀로 할게요. 걱정 마세요.
examples.trans: I will keep it an absolute secret from Cindy. Don't worry.

examples.text: 절대 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (absolutely), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this money?
I was busy today because of money.
I want to open, so right now.
How about trying to open, so together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 반대지, 절대 7은 안 나올 테니까 난 돈은 안 따겠다는 의지지!
examples.trans: Quite the opposite—since it will never sink to seven, it shows my resolve not to take your money!
Here the word for 'is my resolve!' is key.
Did you hear about this youngest member?
I was busy today because of youngest member.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (num).

examples.trans: And our youngest producer Baek Seung-chan wrote 6.8—not even seven?
Here the word for 'six point eight?' is key.
Did you hear about this statistically?
I was busy today because of statistically.

meanings.en: season (of a TV show or sports league)
meanings.note: Loanword from English 'season'.

examples.trans: The new season starts next month.
Last season was really fun.

meanings.note: Prenoun (determiner) placed directly before a noun

examples.trans: Today is my first day at work.
The first snow fell.

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?

meanings.note: Can modify a following noun directly (마지막 촬영지) or take 으로 (마지막으로, 'finally').

examples.trans: Today is the last day.
Please ask the final question.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
Did you hear about this level, degree?
I was busy today because of level, degree.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 통계상 시즌 첫 방송은 전 시즌 마지막 방송보다 2 정도 높았더라고요.
examples.trans: Statistically, a season premiere rated about two points higher than the previous finale.
This expression comes from 'was higher, I found'.

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast, unexpected turn, or new topic. In everyday speech it is very often contracted to 근데. RR: geureonde; spoken geunde.

examples.trans: I contacted them. But there is no reply.
By the way, what time is it now?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 그런데 화창한 날씨라는 변수 때문에 주말 나들이 인구를 감안해서 0.7을 뺐더니.
examples.trans: Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
This expression comes from 'bright and sunny'.
The sky is getting dark and I am anxious to death right now!
The topic of weather came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그런데 화창한 날씨라는 변수 때문에 주말 나들이 인구를 감안해서 0.7을 뺐더니.
examples.trans: Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
Here the word for 'variable' is key.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.
Did you hear about this every weekend?
I was busy today because of every weekend.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그런데 화창한 날씨라는 변수 때문에 주말 나들이 인구를 감안해서 0.7을 뺐더니.
examples.trans: Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
Here the word for 'outing, picnic' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그런데 화창한 날씨라는 변수 때문에 주말 나들이 인구를 감안해서 0.7을 뺐더니.
examples.trans: Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
Here the word for 'population, crowds' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그런데 화창한 날씨라는 변수 때문에 주말 나들이 인구를 감안해서 0.7을 뺐더니.
examples.trans: Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
This expression comes from 'taking into account'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (num).

examples.text: 그런데 화창한 날씨라는 변수 때문에 주말 나들이 인구를 감안해서 0.7을 뺐더니.
examples.trans: Then factoring in weekend outing crowds due to the sunny weather variable, I subtracted 0.7.
Here the word for 'zero point seven' is key.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.
Used in arithmetic.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 백승찬은 해맑은 데가 있어서 호감일 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Baek Seung-chan has an innocent, sunny side, so viewers might really warm up to him.
This expression comes from 'bright and innocent'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이거 봐, 막내는 이래야 되는 거야, 해맑게 긍정적으로!
examples.trans: Look at our youngest writer—this is how a rookie should bet, brightly and positively!
Here the word for 'positively!' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 암튼 내가 그날도 말했지만 공영방송에선 곤란해, 그런 옷.
examples.trans: Anyway, as I said that day too, an outfit like that is trouble on public television.
Here the word for 'anyway' is key.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 암튼 나 이번에 감이 무지 좋아!
examples.trans: Anyway, my gut feeling about this premiere is seriously great!
Here the word for 'gut feeling, intuition' is key.

examples.text: 지는 티 안 내려고 무지 애쓰는데 원래 티가 나는 거예요.
examples.trans: He tries hard not to let it show, but feelings like that always show.

examples.text: 티 안 내려고 무지 애는 쓰시는데 저는 조금 알 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.
Did you hear about this certainty?
I was busy today because of certainty.

meanings.en: to have, to possess, to take
meanings.note: Shortened from 가지다.

examples.trans: I have money on me.
Please bring that here (take it and give).

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
